01

Hot conditions

No altitude correction is needed in hot air for this page. The only question is what the pressure-driven VSI will read for a given true descent.

Groundspeed is calculated: TAS from IAS using air density at the airport (station pressure from QNH and elevation, actual OAT), then groundspeed = TAS − headwind component. ISA temperature at the airport = 15 − 1.98 × elevation / 1,000 (°C). Temperature ratio = (OAT + 273.15) / (ISA at airport + 273.15). A VSI is a pressure-rate instrument, so indicated rate = true rate / ratio, at the entered glide slope angle.

Method & limitations

Built for planning.
Not a substitute for procedure guidance.

The calculator bilinearly interpolates the FAA-published ICAO Cold Temperature Error Table using reported airport temperature and height above airport. Corrections are added to published altitudes; the altimeter setting itself is not changed.

The final descent comparison uses only rows labeled FAF and DA/MDA (or MAP). It derives the nominal distance from their published altitude difference at a 5.2% gradient, then compares that with their cold true-height difference.

A VSI is a pressure-rate instrument. For the displayed cold indication, the app converts geometric vertical speed back to barometric vertical speed using the FAF–DA/MDA layer-thickness ratio from the same cold-correction table. This distinguishes the shallower true path from what the cockpit VSI indicates.

FAA procedures, applicable state rules, operator policy, chart notes, and ATC instructions always take precedence. Coordinate corrections with ATC where required. Baro-VNAV temperature limits are separate.
